APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL ADJOURNED REGULAR MEETING
  OF JANUARY 14, 2020

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE WATER AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:07 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Andre Quintero, Mayor/Chair – present
  Maria Morales, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Jessica Ancona, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Victoria Martinez Muela, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Jerry Velasco, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  m) Mayor Quintero
  s) Councilmember Velasco  5-0

4.  CLOSED SESSION (6:00 p.m. – 7:00 p.m.):

  The City Council and the various Authority Bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council (collectively, the “Council”) will attempt
  to address and complete all Closed Session business between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m.
  If the Council completes all Closed Session business prior to 7:00 p.m., the Council will
  take a short recess and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 7:00 p.m.
  In the event the City Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed
  Session items by 7:00 p.m., the Council will hear all such remaining items toward the
  end of the meeting, immediately following Council Communications. Should any member
  of the public wish to address the Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the
  Council shall allow such person to address the Council on such matter prior to going into
  Closed Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an
  agendized Closed Session matter shall fill out a speaker card and be subject to a
  speaker’s time limit of 3 minutes per speaker and further provided that the Council shall
  be under no obligation to respond to or deliberate upon any specific questions or
  comments posed by a speaker or take action on any issue raised by a speaker beyond
  such action as the City Council may be lawfully authorized to take on an agendized
  Closed Session matter pursuant to the Brown Act (Govt. Code Section 54950 et seq.).

  Howard Owens – Why is the City still negotiating on this property? We discussed that
  maybe you will be placing a park there. We have also discussed what we would like to
  have there. The neighbors in that area do not want a park there. We do not know what
  type of money you will use to purchase this property.

  Ann Ammons – I too am against parks too. There are many transients living at Peck
  Park there and we don’t need this. I really encourage you to place a Police sub-station
  there.

  Mayor Quintero invited members of the public to address the City Council on
  Closed Session Items 4.1 through 4.6.

  Mayor Quintero and the City Council recessed into Closed Session at

8.  PUBLIC COMMENT REGARDING NON-AGENDIZED MATTERS:

  This time has been set aside for persons in the audience to make comments or inquiries
  on matters within the general subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing
  Authority, the Financing Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”)
  that are not listed on this agenda. Although no person is required to provide their
  name and address as a condition to attending a Council meeting, persons who wish to
  address the Council are asked to state their name and address. Each speaker will be
  limited to three (3) continuous minutes. Speakers may not lend any portion of their
  speaking time to other persons or borrow additional time from other persons.

  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.),
  the Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted
  agenda but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent
  meeting. The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for
  consideration at a future meeting.

  All comments or queries presented by a speaker shall be addressed to the Council as a
  body and not to any specific member thereof. No questions shall be posed to any
  member of the Council except through the presiding official of the meeting, the Mayor
  and/or Chair. Members of the Council are under no obligation to respond to questions
  posed by speakers but may provide brief clarifying responses to any comment made or
  questions posed. The Council may not engage in any sort of prolonged discussion or
  deliberation with any speaker or group of speakers on matters that are not listed on this
  agenda.

  Enforcement of Decorum: The Chief of Police, or such member, or members of the
  Police Department as the Chief of Police may designate, shall serve as the Sergeant-at-
  Arms of any Council meeting. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall carry out all orders and
  instructions given by the presiding official for the purpose of maintaining order and
  decorum at the meeting. While members of the public are free to level criticism of City
  policies and the action(s) or proposed action(s) of the Council or its members, members
  of the public may not engage in behavior that is disruptive to the orderly conduct of the
  proceedings, including, but not limited to, conduct that prevents other members of the
  public from being heard when it is their opportunity to speak or which prevents members
  of the audience from hearing or seeing the proceedings. Members of the public may not
  threaten any person with physical harm or act in a manner that may reasonably be
  interpreted as an imminent threat of physical harm. All persons attending the meeting
  must adhere to the City’s policy barring harassment based upon a person’s race,
  religious creed, color, national origin, ancestry, physical handicap, medical condition,
  marital status, gender, sexual orientation or age.
  Xipingeno Zhou – I am here to support the ban on all flavored tobacco products in El
  Monte. These products are appealing to the youth and teenagers. These products
  cause deaths and I hope that my community prevents the selling of these products to
  both the youth and teenagers.

  Yaling Liu – I want to address issues of flavored tobacco. I often can smell menthol in
  our bathrooms at school. Please take action to end the sale of tobacco products.

  3
   City Council Meeting Minutes of January 14, 2020

  Yazhen Liu – I am in favor of banning flavored tobacco.  These flavored tobacco
  products are harmful as traditional tobacco products.

  Gabriel Ramirez – Happy New Year. Congratulations to Vicky for doing a great job at
  the last meeting. I have here the Form 460s for Team El Monte who supports
  candidates. This is a monopoly because this is not working for the people.

  Julio Ramirez – Congratulations Vicky. It is a shame that this City does not follow the
  process like other cities to name their Mayor Pro Tem position.

  Howard Owens – I came back from my vacation that my neighbor’s mail was scattered
  all over the place and opened. Can we meet to discuss this with the post office? Up on

  taken from lock boxes.

  Cosme Jimenez – I think that you are dividing the Council more and more.

  Gabriela Arellanes – I am happy to introduce myself and I am your new representative
  from Assemblywoman Blanca Rubio.

  Mike Gomez – I want to thank the City Council for the great job that you are doing here
  in the City.

18.  COUNCIL COMMUNICATIONS/REPORTS:

  18A.  Mayor Quintero

  If anything about being here at the City is that we get to celebrate two New
  Year’s. We get New Year’s at the beginning of the year and we are going to be
  celebrating Lunar New Year on February 8th Chinese New Year celebration in the
  Downtown Mall area so please come out if you can. I also want to give staff
  thanks for a wonderful 2019 and I know this is going to be a tremendous 2020
  and thank you for all the sacrifices that you make with your families to do what
  you do and thank you very much and City Manager in particular thank you for
  your leadership. City Attorney I hardly recognize you and I do want to say more
  for the community because I am loath to interrupt speakers when they are
  speaking I have been here for 10 years and I can count on one hand how many
  times I have done that. But I have to tell you after a while sometimes it is
  necessary to point out a few things and I want to say I have no problem if we did
  not have contributions put on Forms 460’s there wouldn’t been transparency I
  mean that is a legal requirement and it is there for a purpose for you as residents
  and for those of you who are paying attention at home and for those of you who
  will watch this later on know that there is accountability in place and it is a fair
  comment to be able to make where the resources are coming from for

  9
   City Council Meeting Minutes of January 14, 2020

  candidates for office and usually that is an argument that you make in front of
  voters and not in front of the elected body of here unless to make the following
  point and I think it is a legitimate point the influence of money on politics. This is
  the 10th anniversary of Citizens United and that decision blew a wide door open
  for federal campaign funding. It’s a joy that many would argue had a detrimental
  impact on public policy decision making at the federal level. Obviously we are
  not at the federal level we are at the local level in the 10 years that I have been
  here I have not heard from anyone frankly whose ever said maybe we should
  limit the amount of contributions a candidate receives because as those of you
  who know there are no limits in the City of El Monte. If someone would want to
  drop a million dollars on a campaign here they could. So I am hoping that the
  gentleman who spoke earlier and expressed some concerns about contributions
  will chime in when we have that conversation in the future I anticipate we will
  have conversations about becoming a charter city.

18B.  Mayor Pro Tem Morales

  I wanted to say Happy New Year to everyone who are watching and are present
  at the moment. Like Councilmember Velasco mentioned there is a lot of
  movement in our community with respect to Public Works. I am really looking
  forward to this year being that year that we do see the shovels on the ground and
  we do see a lot of the projects moving along that we were waiting to get going
  and I think it is going to happen this year. We are going to do the best to
  publicize all this movement and if there is traffic that is good traffic because that
  means we are fixing streets and cleaning things up. I am really looking forward
  to that. I wanted to say thank you to staff for putting together and working so
  diligently often times through the weekends and I wanted to let you know it is
  duly noted so thank you for that.

18C.  Councilwoman Ancona

  I want to wish everyone a Happy New Year those of you are still here thank you
  for being here. I hope everyone enjoyed their time off with their families and
  friends over the holidays. Excited over what 2020 will bring we have a lot of
  things going on here in the City of El Monte which we will be sharing with all of
  you in the future. I am also very excited about Fletcher “Fetch” Park this past
  Saturday we just had the renaming of Valley Mall to Main Street. We have a lot
  of improvements going on there and just excited to see what this year will bring.

18D.  Councilwoman Martinez Muela

  Happy New Year everyone 2020 it is an exciting year and hopefully you have a
  lot of exciting plans. This year for me I want to make sure that I stay in touch with
